paragraphs: Baker, here's what I see in Job 27. A man has lost everything, and his friends keep saying he must have earned it. Job says no. He says God has "deprived me of justice," and in the very same breath he swears, "As surely as God lives." He's hurting, he's honest about it, and he still won't let go of God. That's not a man with a perfect faith. That's a man holding on with both hands.

Now look at what Job refuses to do. He will not say his friends are right just to make the pain make sense. He says, "I will maintain my integrity until I die." (Job 27:5) Friend, sometimes the easy road is agreeing with a wrong explanation so everybody can relax. Job won't take it, and he won't lie about himself or about God to get out of the heat.

Then he turns teacher and talks about what happens to the wicked, how their wealth and their houses don't last. Here's the lesson for your own kitchen: what you hold onto matters more than how much you hold. Silver piled up like dust can be gone by morning, but a clear conscience goes everywhere with you. And Job's friends are about to find out this story is far from over, so keep your apron on.
